correctness.summary: The exact tangent-length reduction converts the claim to a four-variable sharp Jensen refinement for tan. Boundary points, all interior local minima, equality, and the degenerating sharpness family are treated analytically; the derived best constant agrees with the limiting quotient.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Ivanova's classical s>=4r inequality and modern square-characterization compilations were distinguished from the new quantitative claim. A 2026 quantitative tangential-polygon result has an angular Jensen deficit in torsional rigidity, but no located source states this sharp semiperimeter/area angle-variance constant or its optimal boundary family. Differently phrased sharp Jensen literature remains a residual risk.

value.summary: The theorem gives a globally sharp quantitative stability strengthening of a classical tangential-quadrilateral inequality, with an explicit optimal constant, equality classification, and sharp degenerating family.

limitations: Only Euclidean convex tangential quadrilaterals are treated.
Stability is measured by interior-angle variance, not Hausdorff distance, side-length variance, or vertex displacement.
The optimal constant is approached by a degenerating family and is not attained by a proper nonsquare quadrilateral.
No optimal-constant claim is made for general tangential N-gons.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; an equivalent sharp Jensen refinement may exist under unrelated terminology.
